form.intro: Write your method down clearly: the knowbot's logic comes only from what you write. Where something is missing we will ask you rather than fill it in.
form.title: Name

q.steps: What are the steps, and which rule decides each step?
q.outputs: What does the output look like?

form.casesHint: Give a few examples whose answers you know: what to ask, and what an item in the result should be. Only you can fill in the expected values (for example, figures you looked up in an annual report); we do not fill them in for you. Testing checks that it runs correctly, not the method itself.

form.rowWhere: Select a row (optional JSON object of column values)

form.rowMatch: Select exactly one row matching {where}, then check {field}. Missing or duplicate rows fail.
form.consent: I agree that the materials I choose in knowbase for testing may be used to test this knowbot. Tests run on my own computer with my own model key. The write-ups and step results are shown only to me; when I ask the platform to test or review it, they are also shown to the platform staff doing that work, to check the knowbot works correctly. They are not used for training, not shown to other users and not used for anything else. They are deleted 90 days after the candidate is listed or replaced by a newer one.

formalExecution.title: Execute validation
formalExecution.hint: Test inputs and expected assertions are saved separately. Assertions are checked after execution. Runs use the selected computer and budget and wait here for approvals. MCP calls require a reviewed zero incremental cost. Metered scripts and model usage are priced separately.
formalExecution.unsupported: Trials support zero-turn direct MCP methods, host-only isolated scripts, licensed single-turn instructions and eligible fixed host workflows.
formalExecution.instructionValidation: Select your registered instruction version or a licensed Skill instruction. The host runs one model turn. The method cannot request additional tools or approvals.
formalExecution.instructionTrial: Each repetition sends the instructions and case inputs to the configured model once. The platform checks the suite budget before dispatch and charges for actual usage. Expected results and assertions stay with the evaluator.
formalExecution.missingPromiseCase: Select a successful test case for each delivery promise.
formalExecution.assertionHint: Use equals, approx or contains with a JSON Pointer. Example: ['{'"kind":"equals","pointer":"/ok","value":true'}']. At least one assertion is required.
formalExecution.computersFailed: Could not load computers. Refresh and try again.
formalExecution.nextVersion: Edit the next version of this suite
formalExecution.unsafeInteger: The browser can enter integers from -9007199254740991 through 9007199254740991. Check the inputs and expected results.
formalExecution.invalid: Invalid suite or settings. Check JSON, caller coverage, model prompts, repetitions and assertions.
formalExecution.failed: Request did not complete ({code}). Refresh its status; execution is never retried automatically.
formalExecution.modelPromptHint: Describe the task and inputs for the model. Keep expected answers in the separate assertions field.
formalExecution.callerCoverage: Each declared caller needs its own successful test case. Model rejection cases support explicit approval denial only.
formalExecution.modelProbe: Model tests allow one outer runtime turn and at most one method call per repetition. The method itself still uses zero internal model turns. A runtime turn may contain several inference requests; model usage counts toward the run budget. Model access and computer readiness are checked by the server.
formalExecution.tracePending: No confirmed model call references yet.
formalExecution.orchestrationHint: Fixed-flow tests support host calls only: every step is required, each has one exact dependency, and failure stops the run. Qualified expert methods can be nested within every level’s declared limits, with at most 100 actual tool calls across the tree. Replanning, model steps and automatic resource bindings remain unsupported. Each external action needs its own approval; approving one step does not approve descendants or later steps. Reloading resumes the same run without replaying completed or unknown calls.

studio.title: Method Studio
studio.lead: Unified Five-Element contract base (Capability · Permissions · Procedure · Validation · Approval) with live Two-View projection.
studio.createTitle: Create a Five-Element draft from an engineering archetype
studio.createLead: Archetypes generate an unlocked engineering skeleton; every business rule must be confirmed by you before trial and freeze.

S1.title: S1 · Deterministic Verification & Calculation
S1.desc: For table reconciliation, structured transforms, and deterministic computation with V0 numeric checks.

S2.title: S2 · Authorized Data Retrieval & Conditional Delivery
S2.desc: For KnowBase reads, conditional routing, and partial-allowed deliverables with citation and coverage checks.

S3.title: S3 · Isolated Blind Review & Cross-Verification
S3.desc: For producer output plus isolated or cross-model-family blind review with V0 gates and bounded reworks.

S4.title: S4 · Controlled External Write / Send Action
S4.desc: For connector writes or external messaging with pre-send prohibited-terms checks and per-action approval.
